articles.title: Electricity with ZERO waste? Scientists just smashed a 30-year record!
articles.summary: Imagine a power cord that never gets hot because electricity flows perfectly. Scientists just made a material that does this at a warmer temperature than ever before—without squeezing it under crazy pressure. They reached 151 Kelvin (about -188°F), breaking a record from 1993.

articles.title: This faraway planet has rock clouds that disappear every night!
articles.summary: On planet WASP-94A b, mornings are cloudy with a chance of rock! But by evening, the clouds vanish. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope spotted this wild weather on a planet 700 light-years away. Scientists think the clouds are made of magnesium silicate—the same stuff in Earth's rocks—and they evaporate in the 1,000-degree heat.

articles.title: A star exploded 440 million years ago—and NASA just found its secret engine!
articles.summary: Some exploding stars shine 10 times brighter than normal. For years, nobody knew why. Now, NASA's Fermi telescope caught gamma rays from a supernova called SN 2017egm, and the evidence points to a magnetar—a super-magnetic, spinning neutron star—as the hidden power source.
